Something to ponder (other than the use of the shift key):

Many of us supposed speedsters solve at a pace that is normal for us.  We complete the puzzle in whatever time it takes to finish the puzzle.  We don't rush; we don't speed.  We just get there faster than others.

Some of us may be blazingly brilliant, but in my case, it's mostly because I have about 45 years of experience, and a wide wheelhouse of general knowledge, both from school and life.  I don't need to slow down because that would be artificial.  It would be like driving 30 on the highway because you're early to the party.  You don't do it.  You drive the normal speed and then sit in your car or take a walk around the block once you get there.

Which is not to say that we don't take time to mull the puzzle over afterwards.  That's why we're here.  I'm on this site several times a day most days.  I focus on things I might have missed while solving.

I get the sense you haven't been solving all that long.  Even if it's five years, or even ten, you might not be able to yet appreciate fully what I mean.  It's like people who say baseball is boring because they don't thoroughly understand it.
